premises.text: Rising deductibles and out-of-pocket costs push consumers to be proactive, yet direct-to-consumer health and wellness lab testing remains largely unavailable and hard to understand
premises.evidence_span: direct-to-consumer testing for health and wellness labs has been virtually untouched in this revolution

premises.text: At-home kits collect blood, saliva, or urine for well-evidenced markers and return understandable results with actionable guidance
premises.evidence_span: convenient, at-home health tests with results you can actually understand

premises.text: Operations use a virtual physician network, CLIA partner labs, multi-state DTC regulatory compliance, and a custom platform that translates HL7 results into a consumer dashboard
premises.evidence_span: a lab requisition was generated, which was then authorized by our virtual physician network

premises.text: Kits sell online at $79–$399, often at or below out-of-pocket/insurance-comparable costs, with planned insurance, corporate wellness, and telemedicine partnerships
premises.evidence_span: We sell our kits online from $79 to $399

value.text: Consumers get convenient, understandable health and wellness lab testing on their own terms
value.evidence_span: Your test, your time, your terms

causal_links.evidence_span: forcing consumers to have to be more proactive with their health decisions
transforming the consumer lab testing experience
as accurate as a test your doctor would order
These costs are actually lower by test than out-of-pocket or not-covered costs per test

notes: Founder fatigue story and paper results folded into the DTC-gap problem framing. Eight kits/expand-to-100 and food-sensitivity/cortisol demo guidance folded as product feature cascade (v1.5.1 §4.1.7). Compliance, physician auth, lab logistics, and HL7 translation kept as one operations platform module. Beta traction metrics excluded. Vision of ubiquitous testing treated as value framing, not a premise.
